anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Loins girded while eating the Passover.
Do not come near a woman — possible frame for sexual abstinence at a holy meal.

pass_a_gloss: The writing then witnessing the loin to lie upon intercourse, we come onto a road of considering what about the pascha it wants us to eat having the loins girded according to kinships. We are commanded, when we chew the pascha, to become clean from bodily coming-together, the girding of the loin signifying this, as it teaches us to bind round the seed-place and commands to stop up the motions of mixing, when we partake of the fleshes of Christ.
pass_b_english: Since then Scripture bears witness that the loin is used of intercourse, we come onto a path of considering what it wants concerning the Passover: that we eat with loins girded according to families. We are commanded, when we chew the Passover, to become clean from bodily coming-together — the girding of the loin signifying this. It teaches us to bind round the seed-place and commands us to stop up the motions of mixing, when we partake of the flesh of Christ.
source_text: Μαρτυρούσης οὖν τῆς γραφῆς τὴν ὀσφὺν ἐπὶ συνουσίας κεῖσθαι εἰς ὁδὸν ἐρχόμεθα τοῦ κατανοεῖν <τί> περὶ τὸ πάσχα περ[ι]εζωμένους ἡμᾶς τὰς ὀσφύας θέλει ἐσθίειν κατὰ συγγενείας. Κελευόμεθα, ὅτε τρώγομεν|| τὸ πάσχα, <καθαροὶ γενέσθαι> ἀπὸ συνελεύσεως σωματικῆς, τῆς περιζώσεως τῆς ὀσφύος τοῦτο σημαινούσης, ὥ[ς] περικαταδῆσαι ἡμᾶς τὸν σπερματικὸν τόπον διδάσκει κ[α]ὶ ἐμφράξαι τὰ τῆς μίξεως κινήματα κελεύει, ὅτε τῶν σαρκῶν μεταλαμβάνομεν [το]ῦ Χ(ριστο)ῦ.
